result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a marked zebra crosswalk and continuous sidewalks on both sides. While the environment provides basic pedestrian infrastructure, safety is reduced by parked cars that obstruct sightlines and a lack of visible traffic control devices at the crossing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked immediately adjacent to the crosswalk on both sides of the street block the line of sight between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Curb sides at the entrance to the marked crosswalk

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: There is no stop sign or signal to regulate vehicle flow at this marked crossing, relying entirely on driver yielding behavior.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the crossing to shorten the pedestrian exposure distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Install high-visibility pedestrian crossing signs or Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB) to alert drivers to the crossing.

result.summary: The image shows a wide residential street with a sidewalk on the left and a park on the right. The environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings and features significant visual obstructions due to continuous on-street parking on both sides.

hazards.description: Continuous lines of parked vehicles on both sides of the street block sightlines between pedestrians attempting to cross and oncoming drivers.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks over a relatively wide street increases pedestrian exposure and provides no clear right-of-way for crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions

interventions.description: Implement speed humps or speed cushions to reduce vehicle speeds on this wide residential corridor.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained sidewalk adjacent to a public park with a paved internal pathway. While the pedestrian space within the park and on the sidewalk is high quality, there is a lack of formal crossing infrastructure, such as marked crosswalks or curb ramps, where the park path meets the street.

hazards.name: Lack of ADA accessibility
